chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Ali ibn Sayf, from Abd al-Mu'min, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: Whoever performs the Hajj pilgrimage fifty times, God will build for him a city in the Garden of Eden, containing one hundred thousand palaces; in each palace there is one of the houri-eyed women and one thousand wives, and he will be made among the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) in Paradise.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing the Hajj pilgrimage fifty times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), emphasizing the cumulative spiritual merit of repeated devotion, where fifty Hajjs result in a unique celestial abode and companionship with the Prophet. This reward underscores the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of consistent ritual practice, linking the pilgrim’s earthly efforts directly to eternal proximity with the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 23-3 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Ali ibn Sayf, on the authority of Abdul Moe’min, on the authority of Harun ibn Kharijah, that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,

“God will build a city in Paradise for whoever goes on the Hajj pilgrimage fifty times. In that city there will be one-hundred thousand palaces, and there will be one of the houri-eyed women of Paradise23 and one-thousand women in each palace. He will be one of Muhammad’s (MGB) friends in Paradise.”
